decisions.reason: As a sports-system extension that sits outside the firm's style-led residential flooring trajectory, it is likely to fall below aspiration levels and be cut as management reallocates resources to stronger core lines.

A mobile arena floor is a niche, adjacent offer with weaker fit to the firm's main customers and future direction, so boundedly rational management would likely drop it if results stayed uncertain or below target.
Because it overlaps with another mobile arena-floor launch and remains distant from the firm's main design-oriented business, it faces a high chance of being removed in a portfolio rationalisation.
The chevron hardwood parquet line is close to the established offer and well aligned with trend-led natural interiors, so it is likely to meet or exceed aspiration levels and be retained.

This squash-court surface finish is a narrow specialist product outside the firm's central market focus, making it a likely candidate for exit if its performance disappoints relative to core flooring products.
Although inexpensive to carry, oak skirting for sports floors depends on a sports-flooring niche that appears peripheral to the firm's strategy, so it is likely to be discontinued with that segment.
